title: When treatments create new conditions | Science
description: When the actor Sam Neill died unexpectedly in July this year, media reports emphasized that his death was not due to cancer. Neill was diagnosed in 2022 with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a form of blood cancer commonly treated with chemotherapy combining as many as five different anticancer drugs. Although initially successful, after four years in remission he stopped responding to chemotherapy. At that point he entered a clinical trial testing the effectiveness of CAR (chimaeric antigen receptor) T-cell therapy in this type of cancer. In CAR T-cell therapies, which have been approved for blood cancers, the patient’s own T cells are genetically modified to recognize and destroy the cancer cells in their body. Neill seems to have responded well, and in April 2026 he publicly announced that he was “cancer-free.” Yet only four months later he was dead, and many people were puzzled about what had “gone wrong.”
